title: docs: document tool-calling compatibility differences (payload + streaming)
author: Ibrahim Khan
release_notes: Docs only: Adds an OpenAI-compat tool-calling + streaming differences page and updates existing README callouts to prevent examples from implying unsupported semantics.
description:
## Summary
Adds explicit compatibility notes for tool calling when using Redwood via the OpenAI-compatible surface area. This is primarily a docs change, but it closes the gap that caused a few recent “copy/paste” examples (in Redwood docs + community snippets) to imply behaviors that the compat layer either doesn’t support or intentionally normalizes.

## Motivation
We saw repeated confusion around:
- Payload shape differences (e.g., `function_call` vs `tool_calls`, presence/absence of `id`, what’s required in tool result messages)
- Streaming behavior during tool calls (partial arguments, ordering, when `finish_reason` arrives)
- Expectations around “parallel tool calls” and mixing assistant text + tool calls in the same streamed turn

These misunderstandings showed up in support tickets (SUP-18421, SUP-18452) and in the DevEx parity audit work (ENG-4821). This PR documents the reality so that Redwood examples/docs can safely link to a canonical compat note and avoid overpromising.

## What’s included
- New page: `docs/compat/tool-calling.md`
  - Side-by-side examples of request/response payloads
  - Streaming transcripts showing partial tool args and final assembly expectations
  - Explicit “Not supported / differs from OpenAI” callouts
- Updates to `README.md` and `docs/compat/streaming.md` to link to the new tool-calling page
- Adds a small “Known pitfalls” section tailored to compat users (partial args, JSON parse, tool result role)

## Key compatibility notes captured
- **Tool call representation:** The compat layer accepts OpenAI-style `tools` and returns `tool_calls` on assistant messages; legacy `function_call` is not documented and should not be used in new examples.
- **Tool call IDs:** `tool_call_id` is required for tool result messages; some models omit/rename fields in intermediate streaming chunks, so examples must assemble the final `tool_call_id` and `arguments` from deltas before invoking tools.
- **Streaming partial args:** `arguments` may be streamed as partial JSON fragments; clients must not `json.loads()`/`JSON.parse()` until the tool call is complete.
- **Parallel tool calls:** Multiple tool calls can appear in one assistant turn, but ordering/streaming interleaving is model-dependent. Examples should treat tool calls as an array and iterate deterministically after finalization.
- **Mixing content + tool calls:** Do not assume assistant `content` will be present alongside `tool_calls` in the same message. Some backends emit empty content when tool calls are present.
- **Finish reasons:** `finish_reason` may arrive only on the final chunk; streaming consumers should not rely on early `finish_reason` to decide that tool args are complete.

## Why this lives in redwood-openai-compat
We want a single source of truth for compat-specific constraints, so the main docs/SDK repos can link out instead of duplicating nuanced edge cases (which then diverge). This also makes it easier to keep up with changes in the compat adapter.

## Testing
- `pnpm lint` (docs)
- `pnpm test` (link checker)
- Manual verification of code blocks against the current compat adapter behavior using the internal “golden transcript” fixture referenced in ENG-4822

## Follow-ups
- Update redwood-docs tool-calling guide to include a short compat callout + link to this page (tracked in ENG-4826)
- Ensure SDK examples that mention OpenAI compat default to the “assemble deltas, then parse” pattern

Checklist:
- [x] Docs have explicit “differs from OpenAI” callouts
- [x] Streaming example avoids parsing partial JSON
- [x] Links validated (no redirects introduced)
- [x] PM terminology matches PM-412 signoff (uses “structured output” vs “JSON mode” consistently where referenced)

review_conversation:
Brian Murphy (review): The callout about `function_call` is good, but be explicit that we don’t guarantee accepting legacy `function_call` requests through compat. People will copy/paste. Also, in the tool result example, please show the `tool` role message with `tool_call_id` (not a made-up `tool_result` role).

Ibrahim Khan (author): Good catch. Updated language to “not supported / not documented” and changed the tool result snippet to use `role: "tool"` + `tool_call_id`.

Wei Chen (review): Can we add one line that warns against assuming content+tool_calls co-exist? This is a frequent docs comment.

Ibrahim Khan (author): Added a dedicated bullet + updated the streaming transcript to show empty `content` while tool calls are being emitted.

Dana Lo (review): In the TypeScript ecosystem, folks parse `arguments` per chunk. Please add a short snippet that shows buffering/assembling. Doesn’t need to be language-specific, but a pseudocode block helps.

Ibrahim Khan (author): Added “assembly pseudocode” section and linked the canonical event nomenclature doc (internal) for future alignment.

Brian Murphy (final): Approving. This should reduce the number of ‘tool args truncated mid-stream’ tickets we’ve been seeing.
